interpretation_summary.overall_judgment: The rule-based semantic comparison is directionally correct: run_0001 is the better research-aligned run, while run_0003 is semantically off-task despite stronger evaluator metrics.
interpretation_summary.metric_success_vs_task_semantic_success: run_0003 shows metric success relative to run_0001 and to its baseline comparison, but task-semantic failure because the produced skill and failure summary both indicate it did not use the renewable inverter control space. run_0001 shows weaker metrics but better semantic alignment with the stated renewable reactive optimization intent.
interpretation_summary.research_meaning: The important research meaning is not merely that the shunt strategy 'lost semantically'; it is that the comparison exposes a divergence between evaluator-facing metric improvement and research-intent alignment.

evidence: run_0003 wins all listed metrics: lower loss, lower voltage deviation, fewer constraint violations, and zero reactive_support_effort

agreements: The baseline correctly treats run_0001 as the research-preferred option.
The baseline correctly identifies a method-family and control-signature mismatch between the two runs.

disagreements_or_corrections: The free-text summary should not imply that run_0003 is a pure performance failure. The listed artifacts show metric improvement, so the more precise reading is: metric success combined with task-semantic mismatch.

The label 'successful' for run_0001 should be read narrowly as semantic/task alignment success, not as proof of full engineering adequacy, because the artifacts still show nonzero constraint violations and no evaluator threshold information.

new_insights: run_0003 is valuable as a negative-control result: it demonstrates that a strategy can improve evaluator-facing metrics while remaining semantically misaligned with the intended renewable control problem.

The comparison suggests an evaluator-intent gap: zero reactive_support_effort and better metrics were still achievable without using renewable inverter control, so metric superiority alone is insufficient to establish task success.
run_0001 should be preferred for research not because it is numerically best, but because it exercises the intended control family and therefore produces more reusable task-aligned knowledge.
overclaim_warnings: Do not claim that run_0003 failed on performance metrics; the comparison artifact shows the opposite.
Do not claim that run_0001 fully solved the renewable reactive optimization problem; the artifacts only support that it is the more task-aligned run.
Do not infer a detailed physical mechanism for why inverter support should win; the listed artifacts show alignment and mismatch, not causal proof.
Do not generalize from this pairwise comparison to a broader rule about all shunt-based methods or all renewable-aware methods.
missing_evidence: No task package or evaluator rationale is included in the input refs, so it cannot be verified whether using inverter-Q control was mandatory, strongly preferred, or only one acceptable solution family.
No control trace or dispatch artifact is included beyond summary notes, so the depth of actual inverter coordination cannot be assessed.
No evaluator thresholds or baseline artifact are included, so 'completed' and 'improved' cannot be translated into absolute adequacy claims.

recommended_action.primary: Keep run_0001 as the preferred-for-research result.
recommended_action.reporting_change: Revise semantic reporting language from any form of 'performance failure' to 'metric improvement with task-semantic mismatch'.
recommended_action.schema_or_analysis_change: Add an explicit dimension such as 'metric_task_divergence' or 'intent_alignment_gap' so future comparisons can record when evaluator metrics and research intent separate.
recommended_action.claim_boundary: Use this comparison as evidence of control-space mismatch and evaluator blind-spot risk, not as evidence that inverter-support is globally superior in performance.
